state.case_summary:
A 53-year-old man reported substernal chest pain, lasting less than 5 minutes, which sometimes occurred if he ran more than 2 miles. Medical history included hypertension (controlled with lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide), LDL of 155 mg/dL, and HDL of 44 mg/dL. He did not smoke and had no family history of premature coronary artery disease.

Physical examination results were unremarkable. Blood pressure was 134/80 mm Hg, body mass index was 26, and resting electrocardiogram (ECG) results were normal.

- Exercise Treadmill Test (ETT):  - Patient had no chest pain during ETT  - ST depressions occurred during recovery phase  - Patient demonstrated high exercise capacity- Subsequent Testing:  - CCTA (Computed Tomography Angiogram): Demonstrated 3-vessel involvement  - PET-MPI (Positron Emission Tomography-Myocardial Perfusion Imaging): Showed severe ischemia in the distribution of the left anterior descending and circumflex arteries  - Coronary Angiogram: Confirmed findings
